villain.justification: The claim that a 101-year-old woman gave birth to her 17th child is a verified viral hoax. The individuals in the photograph are actually Rosa Camfield and her newborn great-granddaughter, Kaylee Rowland. The image was taken in March 2015 by Camfield's granddaughter, Sarah Hamm, to capture a family moment. The narratives involving a 17th child and a cancer diagnosis are completely fabricated details added to the image to increase social media engagement. Furthermore, multiple fact-checking organizations, including Vishvas News and VERA Files, have debunked the claim, noting that the hoax often incorrectly conflates this personal family photo with unrelated medical cases involving late-life pregnancies.

qa_pairs.answer: The narrative is a complete fabrication. There is no evidence that Rosa Camfield had 16 children or that she gave birth following a cancer diagnosis; these details were added to the image to create a viral hoax.

statements.statement: The woman in the photo is not a 101-year-old woman who gave birth, but an American named Rosa Camfield holding her great-granddaughter Kaylee Rowland, in a photo taken by Sarah Hamm, who is the mother of Kaylee Rowland and the granddaughter of Rosa Camfield, which originally went viral in March 2015 after being posted by the Facebook page 'Life of Dad'.

While the image (CLAIM_IMG_0) does depict an elderly woman holding a baby, evidence shows that the woman is actually Rosa Camfield and the infant is her great-granddaughter, Kaylee Rowland. The photo was taken by Sarah Hamm, who is the mother of the baby and the granddaughter of the elderly woman. The claim is a fabrication; similar hoaxes involving this image have circulated previously, including false claims that the woman was an Italian named Anatolia Vertadella who gave birth via an ovary transplant.
